ratings_why.fun: Every buy is a timing question, and seating Cutters, Three Ears and Old Wat on the zigzag gives real puzzles each turn; the dark turns and a bland Tier 1 keep it from an 8.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns the 8 because the reset is a resource, not a penalty: you Wax into the New Moon on purpose, cash lost light as gold, or lend it to Jacks and other tribes, and no current tribe treats time like that.

verdict_why: The core Full Moon combo depends on trigger order that the rules don't state; once that is written down it should settle.

points.text: Full Moon trigger order is unstated: Build A relies on the Moon-Scour resolving before Chalk-Cutter in reading order, and Dame Waxwell could mean each effect twice in place or the whole set twice. Say which, since it changes the total several times over.
Dew-Pond Scryer is the best decision card in the tribe: play it on Waxing to reach Full, or on Waning to reset on your terms. A second cheap Wax source at Tier 1 would open the Fast Moon earlier.
Spring-Ring Jill is the only card that ignores the Moon's other uses. Let it box a Jack beside it, giving that Jack the stats instead, so the boxing theme meets the Lending House early.
March Madcap's random target wastes the seating game; give the light to the Hare behind or beside the one that died so you can plan it.
Leveret's relay into a Hare after the reset quietly makes light last a whole cycle; a later card that rewards that relay chain (Leveret into Leveret into Old Wat) would be a lovely hidden combo.

standouts.why: A Jack who isn't a Hare is the tribe's loophole to its own law, and Silverpenny copying him to keep light for a cycle is a combo the card doesn't spell out.
A multiplier whose value is all in seating: the middle of the zigzag touches four Hares, and order against the Moon-Scour matters.
One word of text, but it bends the whole cycle and turns the New Moon into a play you choose.

weakest.why: A plain When played buff with a phase bonus; it does one obvious job.
Random, fight-only and needs lit Hares to die, so it rarely joins the planned combos.
Necessary insurance for the dark turns, but it is a stat block with Shield and no interplay.

flags.note: How Waxwell's repeat orders against other Full Moon effects isn't written, and the Scour-before-Cutter order isn't in the rules.
Golden Waxwell with golden Chalk-Cutters can reach thousands of light for a fight; capped by the reset but a one-fight kill.
Mother banks half of a multiplied cycle permanently on Jacks and other tribes, and the Scour counter grows the amount each cycle, faster with a Fast Moon.
With Moon-Caller and Full Moon doubling, a fresh Hare can sell for 4 and Wax each turn; once-a-turn should hold it, but check with cheap shop buffs.
